newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy banks cautious on Olivetti exposure.
newsitem.headline: Italy banks cautious on Olivetti exposure.

text.p: Two of Italy's largest banks were cautious on their debt exposure to the troubled information technology group Olivetti, and denied figures published in Italian newspapers on their loans to the loss-making group.

Italy's largest bank San Paolo said its loans to Olivetti were not as high as the 400-600 billion lire quoted in some newspapers. A bank spokesman said the numbers were not correct and were lower than those indicated in the papers.

Another top Italian bank Banca Commerciale Italiana also denied newspaper reports that its loans to Olivetti were 200-300 billion lire or as high as 400 billion in one paper. A bank spokesman said the figures given in the papers did not correspond to the real situation.

Earlier this week, Olivetti reported first half 1996 results showing continued losses, deeper debts while its director general in charge of finance, administration and auditing resigned this week over his misgivings about the accuracy of the the company's accounts.
